slides.title: Advertising and Persuasion
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 8 English, Unit 4: Advertising and Persuasion. Every day, you are surrounded by messages designed to grab your attention, change your mind, or convince you to buy something. From billboards towering over busy Mogadishu streets to sponsored posts sliding through your social media feed, advertising is everywhere. But how does it work? What techniques do advertisers use to persuade people? And how can you, as a critical thinker, tell the difference between honest information and clever manipulation? In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and understand passages about advertising techniques, persuasion, and ethical marketing, and discuss their ideas confidently. You will also identify and use prepositions preceding nouns correctly in phrases like on sale, in stock, for a limited time, at a discount, and with interest. You will also form and use passive voice sentences in the present and past: "The product was launched by the company" and "The advert is designed to attract young people." Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: aptitude, adversary, cunning, momentum, bonanza, concession. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Adverts Everywhere: An Interview about Advertising Ethics
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Power of Persuasion and Adverts Everywhere: An Interview about Advertising Ethics. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Prepositions Preceding Nouns

slides.narration: The first language focus is Prepositions Preceding Nouns. Prepositions are small words that show the relationship between a noun and the rest of the sentence. In advertising language they sit directly before nouns to build fixed phrases such as on sale, in stock and at a discount, and learning each phrase as one complete unit makes your English sound natural and precise. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: My Advertising Story. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
